- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early periods of a 30-day forecast (e.g., first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast values.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.2 → +0.4), model fails to capture mean reversion; apply slight downward bias in middle-to-late forecast.  
- When sentiment is flat or low (0.0–0.4), model often ignores trend; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to reflect muted market sentiment.  
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 10 days of 30-day horizon; apply smoothing or lag correction (e.g., average last 5 days) for early periods.
